es: Usar adjetivos evaluativos académicos (robust, flawed, compelling, tentative) para valorar un estudio con su razón, y reconocer la pasiva impersonal.

vocabulary.es: sólido, resistente (un resultado que se mantiene)
no alcanzar, quedarse corto respecto a

teaching.en: The results are robust: the sample was large, the method was clear, and the finding survived a second attempt.
teaching.es: Los resultados son sólidos: la muestra era grande, el método era claro y el hallazgo resistió un segundo intento.
teaching.explanationEs: Robust valora bien un resultado que se mantiene en distintas pruebas; la razón va tras los dos puntos.
segments: The results are robust: the sample was large, the method
was clear, and the finding survived a second attempt.
teaching.audioText: The results are robust: the sample was large, the method was clear, and the finding survived a second attempt.

teaching.en: A flawed design can cast doubt on every result that follows from it, however impressive the figures may look.
teaching.es: Un diseño con fallos puede sembrar dudas sobre todos los resultados que se derivan de él, por impresionantes que parezcan las cifras.
teaching.explanationEs: Cast doubt on es la colocación para debilitar la confianza en algo; however + adjetivo concede el atractivo de las cifras.
segments: A flawed design can cast doubt on every result that
follows from it, however impressive the figures may look.
teaching.audioText: A flawed design can cast doubt on every result that follows from it, however impressive the figures may look.

teaching.en: The evidence is compelling, since three independent teams found the same effect, and their combined data lend weight to the claim.
teaching.es: La evidencia es convincente, ya que tres equipos independientes hallaron el mismo efecto, y sus datos combinados dan peso a la afirmación.
teaching.explanationEs: Lend weight to significa «respaldar»; data se usa aquí como plural, por eso lend y no lends.
segments: The evidence is compelling, since three independent teams found the same
effect, and their combined data lend weight to the claim.
teaching.audioText: The evidence is compelling, since three independent teams found the same effect, and their combined data lend weight to the claim.

teaching.en: It is widely believed that coffee sharpens memory, but the authors stay tentative about one small study.
teaching.es: Se cree ampliamente que el café agudiza la memoria, pero los autores se muestran prudentes ante un solo estudio pequeño.
teaching.explanationEs: Repaso de la pasiva impersonal (it is believed that…) junto a tentative, que marca la cautela de los autores.
segments: It is widely believed that coffee sharpens memory, but
the authors stay tentative about one small study.
teaching.audioText: It is widely believed that coffee sharpens memory, but the authors stay tentative about one small study.

teaching.en: Even a thorough study can leave the proof far from conclusive if its methods fall short of accepted standards.
teaching.es: Incluso un estudio minucioso puede dejar la prueba lejos de ser concluyente si sus métodos no alcanzan los estándares aceptados.
teaching.explanationEs: Thorough elogia el cuidado; conclusive dice que la cuestión queda cerrada; fall short of = no llegar al nivel exigido.
segments: Even a thorough study can leave the proof far from
conclusive if its methods fall short of accepted standards.
teaching.audioText: Even a thorough study can leave the proof far from conclusive if its methods fall short of accepted standards.

teaching.en: Questionable wording may call into question an otherwise methodologically sound survey, because respondents can read the items differently.
teaching.es: Una redacción dudosa puede poner en entredicho una encuesta por lo demás metodológicamente correcta, porque los encuestados pueden leer las preguntas de otro modo.
teaching.explanationEs: Questionable es un adjetivo de cautela; call into question = poner en entredicho; otherwise = por lo demás.
segments: Questionable wording may call into question an otherwise methodologically
sound survey, because respondents can read the items differently.
teaching.audioText: Questionable wording may call into question an otherwise methodologically sound survey, because respondents can read the items differently.

prompt.es: Completa: «Por eso, el diseño del estudio tiene graves fallos.»

feedback.es: Flawed describe un diseño con fallos; la razón (muestra pequeña y elegida por amigos) está en la frase anterior.

hint.es: Adjetivo que señala un fallo de diseño y termina en -ed.

origin.text: Only twelve students took part, and all of them were chosen by the researcher's friends. For that reason, the design of the study is seriously ___.

prompt.es: Elige la valoración que combina el resultado y la actitud de los autores.

choices.text: The findings look flawed, since the authors call for further trials.
The findings look robust, so the authors sound conclusive.
The findings look robust, while the authors stay tentative.

feedback.es: El mismo patrón en seis países sugiere resultados sólidos, pero los autores escriben solo «may» y piden más ensayos: son prudentes.

hint.es: Un patrón repetido suena sólido; «may» y «further trials» suenan prudentes.

origin.text: A survey of five thousand adults in six countries found the same pattern each time. The authors, however, write only that it may indicate a link, and they call for further trials before drawing any firm conclusion.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Una muestra tan pequeña siembra dudas sobre todo el estudio.»

answer.text: Such a small sample casts doubt on the whole study

feedback.es: Such a + adjetivo + sustantivo pone el énfasis en el tamaño; casts doubt on sigue a un sujeto singular.

hint.es: Such a va antes del adjetivo y del sustantivo.

prompt.es: Elige el adjetivo que evalúa con precisión cada estudio.

feedback.es: Cada razón apunta a un adjetivo: muestra sesgada, flawed; efecto que resiste cada repetición, robust; argumento al que cuesta oponerse, compelling; primer vistazo, tentative.

sentences: Only ten people took part and the sample was biased, so the design is ___.
The same effect survived every repetition of the test and in every country, so the result is ___.
Three independent teams reached the same view and a careful reader would struggle to disagree, so the case is ___.
The authors call it a first look and ask for more trials, so their conclusion is ___.
origin.text: Four studies reached the college reading group this week. Evaluate each one with the adjective that fits its evidence best: robust, flawed, compelling or tentative.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué opina la hablante del estudio.

choices.text: The method impressed her, but the wording of the survey makes her hesitate.
The method impressed her, but the survey wording leads her to reject the paper completely.
The survey wording worried her, but the method made her fully trust the result anyway.

feedback.es: Elogia el método (thorough), pero duda de las preguntas (questionable) y por eso aplaza su confianza: no rechaza el estudio ni lo acepta sin reservas.

origin.audio: I read the whole paper this morning. The method is thorough, since every step is checked and explained. But the survey questions are questionable, so I would not trust the headline result just yet. I would call the conclusions tentative at best.

prompt.es: ¿Qué valoración del experimento es la más precisa?

choices.text: Flawed: a single trial with volunteers can never show anything.
Tentative: a small first trial that hints at a possible benefit.
Conclusive: a small result that already settles the question.

feedback.es: El equipo realizó el experimento una sola vez, con treinta voluntarios, y pide un ensayo mayor: es un resultado provisional, no concluyente.

origin.text: The team ran the experiment once, with thirty volunteers, and reported a small improvement. They write that the data are consistent with a benefit, but that a larger trial is needed before any firm conclusion can be drawn.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender la evaluadora sobre la afirmación principal del estudio?

choices.text: That the statistics are weak and should be repeated by another independent team of researchers.
That the tea obviously has no effect, since the teacher caused the result.
That a comparison group would prove the authors' claim completely.
That careful work does not justify so firm a claim from such limited evidence.

feedback.es: La evaluadora elogia el trabajo, pero señala que una sola aula sin grupo de comparación no basta para una afirmación tan firme.

origin.text: Reviewer's report: The authors have plainly worked hard. Their survey is thorough, and their statistics are handled with care. Yet the headline claim, that green tea improves concentration, rests on a single classroom in one school, with no comparison group. One is left wondering whether the tea, the teacher or the time of day made the difference.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué quiere enseñar la profesora sobre cómo valorar un estudio pequeño.

choices.text: That a judgement is fair only when the claim is no bigger than the evidence.
That a small sample is an acceptable reason to call any study flawed.
That honest authors should avoid tentative language to sound more convincing.
That a study should be evaluated by the size of its sample and nothing else.

feedback.es: La profesora dice que un estudio pequeño puede ser honesto si sus afirmaciones son prudentes; el fallo está en la distancia entre evidencia y afirmación.

origin.audio: When you evaluate a study, do not reach for the strongest word. Calling a study flawed because its sample is small is fair only if the authors claim more than that sample allows. A small study that says tentative things can be perfectly honest. Suppose two teams each test forty people. One team writes that the medicine always works; the other writes that the result is encouraging and deserves a larger trial. Their data may be the same, and yet only the first team has gone too far. The real fault is a claim that is bigger than its evidence.

prompt.es: Completa: «El segundo informe no alcanzó el nivel exigido.»

feedback.es: Fall short of es la colocación para «no alcanzar» un nivel o estándar.

origin.text: The committee read all three reports with care. The second, however, fell ___ of the standard required, because it gave no details of how the participants were chosen.

prompt.es: Valora el estudio en dos frases: resultado, razón y actitud de los autores.

answer.text: The results are robust and the method is thorough, since three thousand people in five countries showed the same pattern. Even so, the authors remain tentative and call for more trials before any firm conclusion is drawn.
accepted: The results are robust and the method is thorough, since three thousand people in five countries showed the same pattern. Even so, the authors remain tentative and call for more trials before any firm conclusion is drawn.
The findings are robust, because people in five countries produced the same result every time. The authors are tentative, however, and ask for further trials before any firm conclusion is drawn.
The evidence is compelling, since 3000 people in five countries gave the same result. Nevertheless, the authors remain cautious and call for more trials.

feedback.es: Un buen comentario combina un adjetivo preciso, la razón con datos del estudio y la cautela de los autores.

origin.text: Datos: 3000 participantes de cinco países; el mismo resultado en cada réplica del experimento; método revisado paso a paso. Los autores escriben que sus conclusiones son provisionales y piden más ensayos.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito escribe el autor este párrafo?

choices.text: To warn readers that late meals are dangerous for their sleep and their general health.
To show that a popular idea is not the same as a proven one.
To argue that thirty trials are too few to decide anything.
To defend late meals against unfair reviews of the evidence.

feedback.es: El autor no dice que cenar tarde sea bueno ni malo: señala que una idea puede ser popular y reconfortante sin estar respaldada por pruebas.

origin.text: It is widely believed that eating late at night ruins sleep, and advice columns repeat it every winter. Yet a review that pooled thirty trials found no clear effect. The reviewers do not say that late meals are good for you; they say the evidence is simply not there. A claim can be popular, old and comforting without ever becoming well supported.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los datos no son concluyentes, pero el estudio es minucioso.»

answer.text: The data are not conclusive, yet the study is thorough
accepted: The data are not conclusive, yet the study is thorough
The study is thorough, yet the data are not conclusive

feedback.es: Yet introduce el contraste: lo minucioso del estudio no basta para que los datos sean concluyentes.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada fórmula evaluativa con su sentido.

feedback.es: Las cuatro fórmulas sirven para valorar: respaldar, poner en entredicho, no alcanzar y sembrar dudas.
